strategy.summary: GET /products (src/app.js listProducts) filters the in-memory catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages with `limit` (default 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT) and `offset`, returns { total, items }, and refuses non-whole or limit<1 values with 400. Integration tests start the real http server on an OS-chosen port (as test/products.test.js does) and assert search, paging, total, the cap and the refusals.
inScope: limit/offset paging, total, default and capped limit
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
assumptions: The code's cap MAX_LIMIT = 50 is correct and the README's 'up to 100' is stale (asked as Q1); tests import MAX_LIMIT and DEFAULT_LIMIT from src/app.js rather than hardcoding.

Expected matches are derived from the exported PRODUCTS catalogue (src/catalogue.js) with the same filter in the test for counts only where needed; concrete names/ids are asserted where the catalogue is fixed (e.g. 'kettle' matches the 15 Kettle products).
The server runs for real in-process on port 0; nothing is faked. GET /products doesn't mutate state, so sharing one server per file is safe.
openQuestions: README says limit goes up to 100; code caps at 50. Which is intended? (Q1)

risks.description: Cap value differs between README and code
risks.mitigation: Test asserts the cap the code exports and flags the README conflict

risks.description: Paging off-by-one or total counting only the page
risks.mitigation: Assert exact ids of a middle page and that total is the full match count, not the page size

risks.description: Validation lets through decimals/negatives/0 producing odd slices
risks.mitigation: Table of invalid values each asserted 400

acceptanceCriteria.text: q matches products whose name contains it, case-insensitively; without q every product is listed.
Results are paged by limit and offset, the response includes the total number of matches, and limits above the maximum are capped.
A limit or offset that isn't a whole number, or a limit below 1, is refused with 400.

testCases.title: matches names containing q regardless of case
testCases.expected: 200; total 15; every item name starts with 'Kettle '; ids are the 15 Kettle products

testCases.title: matches q anywhere in the name, not only at the start
testCases.expected: 200; total 15; all items are 'Tea strainer N'
testCases.rationale: Proves substring rather than prefix match

testCases.title: returns no items and a total of 0 when nothing matches
testCases.rationale: Search with no hits must not error

testCases.title: lists every product when q is omitted
testCases.expected: 200; total equals PRODUCTS.length (120); items are the first DEFAULT_LIMIT products by id
testCases.rationale: Unfiltered listing and default page size

testCases.title: returns the requested page with the total of all matches
testCases.expected: 200; total 30 (Teapot + Tea strainer); items are the 11th-20th matches in id order
testCases.rationale: Paging combined with search; total is full match count, not page size

testCases.title: returns no items for an offset past the last match
caps a limit above the maximum
refuses a limit or offset that isn't a whole number, or a limit below 1, with 400
steps: For each of limit=0, limit=-1, limit=2.5, limit=abc, limit=(empty), offset=-1, offset=1.5, offset=abc: GET /products with it
testCases.expected: Each is 400 with a JSON body that has an error field

testCases.title: accepts a limit of 1 and an offset of 0
testCases.expected: 200; items is just product id 1; total 120

strategy.environmentNotes: No services needed; the app is started in-process with createApp().listen(0). Runs under the existing `npm test` (vitest run).

questions.question: The README says GET /products `limit` goes "up to 100", but the code caps it at MAX_LIMIT = 50 (src/app.js). Which cap is correct?
questions.assumption: The code's cap (50, imported as MAX_LIMIT) is correct and the README is stale; tests assert the cap via the imported constant and the README discrepancy goes in a follow-up.
questions.answer: The cap is 50, as the code does. The README is out of date; leave it as it is and test against 50.
